name: Bicuspid Aortic Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Bicuspid Aortic Valve

criteria.description: Presence of two aortic valve leaflets instead of three on imaging
Dilatation of the ascending aorta or aortic root on imaging
Evidence of aortic stenosis or regurgitation on echocardiography

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of bicuspid valve morphology plus at least one major criterion such as valvular dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on echocardiographic visualization of valve morphology and function.

pathognomonic.notes: Heard on auscultation, characteristic of bicuspid valve

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bicuspid aortic valve morphology on echocardiography
searchTerms: bicuspid aortic valve seen on echo

common.notes: Due to progressive aortic stenosis or regurgitation
Secondary to valve dysfunction or aortic pathology
May occur with arrhythmias secondary to valve disease

occasional.notes: May occur with severe aortic stenosis
Variable intensity depending on valve dysfunction

searchTerms: chest pain due to artery enlargement

rare.notes: Embolic event secondary to valve pathology

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; inflammatory markers elevated if infective endocarditis present
imaging: Echocardiography showing two aortic valve leaflets
CT/MRI demonstrating aortic root or ascending aorta dilation
Doppler studies showing aortic stenosis or regurgitation
genetic: Familial clustering reported; NOTCH1 gene mutations associated in some cases
other: Physical exam revealing systolic ejection click and murmur

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of three valve leaflets on imaging
Upper limb hypertension with lower limb hypotension
Imaging showing aortic narrowing distal to left subclavian artery

redFlags: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis symptoms
Signs of aortic dissection (sudden severe chest/back pain)
Evidence of infective endocarditis (fever, positive blood cultures)
references: Michelena HI, et al. Bicuspid Aortic Valve: Identifying Knowledge Gaps and Rising to the Challenge From the International Bicuspid Aortic Valve Consortium (BAVCon). Circulation. 2014.
Tzemos N, et al. Outcomes in adults with bicuspid aortic valves. JAMA. 2008.
Garg V, et al. Mutations in NOTCH1 cause aortic valve disease. Nature. 2005.
